question: What genetic technique could you use to diagnose an Angelman syndrome ?:

options.opb: In situ hybridization with fluorescence (FISH) with centromeric probe.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Conventional cytogenetics (karyotype of G bands) -> Detection of chromosomal abnormalities -> Possible identification of deletion in chromosome 15 -> 70% CHAIN: In situ hybridization with fluorescence (FISH) with centromeric probe -> Detection of chromosome 15 abnormalities -> Identification of Angelman syndrome deletion -> 80% CHAIN: (FISH) with telomeric probe -> Detection of telomeric abnormalities -> Possible indication of Angelman syndrome deletion -> 60% CHAIN: (FISH) with locus-specific probe -> Targeted detection of specific genetic region -> Identification of Angelman syndrome deletion -> 70%
analysis: Angelman syndrome is typically caused by a deletion or mutation on the maternally inherited chromosome 15q11-13 region. Therefore, a genetic technique that can detect this specific deletion or mutation would be most appropriate for diagnosing Angelman syndrome.
